runbooks.diagnosis: PostgreSQL OOM in this stack is almost always shared_buffers/work_mem sized for a bigger tier than the host, or PgBouncer letting in more active connections than max_connections can hold. The OOM killer targets the backend with the largest allocation.
remediation: Check dmesg for which process the OOM killer chose
Compare shared_buffers+work_mem*max_connections against the container memory limit
Lower PgBouncer default_pool_size or postgres max_connections
Restart postgres as a last resort — expect a failover of app connections

runbooks.diagnosis: Connection exhaustion: a service is leaking connections or PgBouncer pool mode does not match the workload (transaction pooling breaks session-level features).
remediation: Identify the leaking client via pg_stat_activity (client_addr counts)
Verify PgBouncer pool_mode matches the service expectations
Restart the leaking service before touching postgres

symptoms: database files are incompatible with server
runbooks.diagnosis: Postgres major version downgrade attempt — the data directory was initialized by a newer major version. The postgres-data volume pins the major version; image tag drift causes this.
remediation: Pin the postgres image back to the major version that created the data dir
Never bump the postgres major without a pg_dump/pg_upgrade migration
